speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS (Abdominal_Ultrasound not requested in data; clinical presentation of paroxysmal crying, distension, and LLQ pain with normal blood work and radiographic findings of obstruction/Hirschsprung disease suggests intermittent colicky pain rather than continuous crying).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception.

(The clinical presentation of paroxysmal crying, abdominal distension, and pain on palpation in an 8-month-old is classic for intussusception, a leading cause of intestinal obstruction in this age group.)
